question: Given the scale of the financial commitments made by issuing debt to finance NextGenerationEU, how important is it to ensure that additional own resources are available so that the European Commission can honour those financial commitments?

Given the timeframe of these financial commitments, when must the necessary legislative acts be approved and come into effect, at both European and national level, to ensure that the additional own resources are available in good time?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.7.2024) 1. The repayment of NextGenerationEU debt (NGEU) is a legal obligation stemming from the Own Resources Decision1, regardless of the outcome of the ongoing discussions on the proposal for new own resources. All liabilities incurred by NGEU will be fully repaid at the latest by 31 December 2058.

The Interinstitutional Agreement of December 2020 provided a roadmap for the introduction of new own resources for which the Commission had already put forward its proposals. As also acknowledged in the Interinstitutional Agreement, new sources of revenue are essential to enable the EU to finance its policies without increasing the national contribution of Member States or reducing spending programmes. 2.

The Commission adopted its proposal in June 20232, one year before what was foreseen in the Interinstitutional Agreement of December 2020. It gave priority to a balanced own resources package that could be adopted as soon as possible. Given the complex process for the approval of the Own Resources Decision, a decision by Member States would be necessary as soon as possible.
The Commission remains committed to supporting ongoing discussions with Member States.
